hints: Each hotel has a remaining capacity, and a group needs one hotel with capacity at least its size.
A segment tree stores the maximum capacity in each interval.
At each request, descend left first where the maximum is large enough, assign that earliest hotel, then reduce its capacity.
analogy: Use interval maximums to skip every block of hotels that cannot fit the next group.
example: Capacities 3,5,4 and request 4 fit the first suitable hotel, index 2; its remaining capacity becomes 1.
algorithm: Build a max segment tree. For request x, if root maximum<x output 0; otherwise descend to the leftmost leaf with value>=x, subtract x, and output its index.
correctness: The left-first descent selects the earliest eligible hotel; the stored maximum proves skipped subtrees contain no fit, and updating the leaf preserves later searches.
complexity: O((n+q) log n) time and O(n) space.
